paragraphs: The development environment setup for Chapter 4 of the Plant Moisture Detection project involves configuring the hardware and software components to ensure proper operation. The framework used is arduino_stm32core, which builds on the STM32 HAL drivers. The programmer will use ST-Link V2 via SWD interface to program the microcontroller. The code stats indicate that the file Plant_Moisture_Detection.ino contains 202 lines of code with 116 code lines written by the user.

The project requires several peripherals and clocks to function properly. The System Core Clock is set to 72 MHz, which is derived from HSE 8 MHz using a PLL x9. APB1 and APB2 prescalers are set to /2 and /1 respectively, providing clock frequencies of 36 MHz and 72 MHz respectively.

The ADC is configured with a prescaler of /6 to achieve a frequency of 12 MHz for the ADCCLK. The soil moisture sensor analog out is connected to PA0 (ADC1_IN0), which measures the voltage at the soil moisture sensor. The onboard status LED is connected to PC13 (GPIOC) and is active-low, indicating when action is needed.

The project also requires a USB-to-UART adapter for serial communication. The RX pin of USART1_TX is connected to PA9, and the TX pin of USART1_RX is connected to PA10. This allows for reliable serial telemetry and debug monitoring at 115200 baud.

To eliminate sensor measurement noise, a moving average filtering technique will be implemented in the code. The filtered values will be used to determine the moisture level and trigger alerts when necessary.
The onboard status LED logic on PC13 needs to be handled correctly. The active-low logic should be inverted using a suitable digital circuit or library function to ensure proper operation.

To avoid spurious state switching, a reliable threshold or hysteresis state evaluation will be implemented in the code. This will help to prevent the system from switching between states unnecessarily and improve overall performance.
